title: Subgroup index and the smallest defining equation
summary: Subgroups, root fields, and faithful permutation actions describe the same degree problem. The equivalences below lead to the complete minimum-degree formula.
scope: Fix a finite Galois extension \(L/K\) with \(G=\operatorname{Gal}(L/K)\cong\operatorname{PSL}_2(\mathbb F_p)\), where \(p\ge5\) is prime. An equation means a separable irreducible polynomial over \(K\) whose splitting field is \(L\). Nodes asserting an object mean that such an object exists.

nodes.label: Faithful transitive action on p points
Degree-p equation with splitting field L

edges.label: Degree equals index
edges.explanation: The Galois correspondence sends H to its fixed field E=L^H and gives [E:K]=[G:H].

edges.label: Cosets and stabilizers
edges.explanation: An index-p subgroup gives a transitive action on its p cosets. Its kernel is the core of H; simplicity makes this kernel trivial. Conversely, a point stabilizer in a transitive degree-p action has index p.

edges.label: Primitive element and normal closure
edges.explanation: A primitive element of E has degree p. The normal closure of E in L is fixed by the core of its stabilizer; simplicity makes that core trivial. Conversely, any root of an irreducible degree-p polynomial generates a degree-p intermediate field.

edges.label: Realize the root action
edges.explanation: For the given extension L/K, the fixed field of a point stabilizer has a primitive element whose conjugates give this faithful action. Conversely, an irreducible polynomial with splitting field L gives a faithful transitive action on its roots.

edges.label: Classical classification
edges.explanation: Through the equivalent subgroup condition, Theorem 2 and the constructions in Section 4 give exactly p=5,7,11. The subgroup classification is classical; the cited exposition is a recent preprint.

sources.note: 2022 book: degree–index formula and primitive element theorem. Printed and PDF page numbers differ by ten.
The normal closure corresponds to the largest normal subgroup contained in H, its core. The coset-action argument is also given below.
Classical simplicity and subgroup theorem, discussed in a 2026 preprint; exceptional constructions make the index-p statement necessary and sufficient.
Faithful root actions and irreducibility versus transitivity. The order-p lower bound is proved directly below.

body:
Corollary of classical Galois theory

For the given extension, let \(d(L/K)\) be the smallest degree of a separable irreducible polynomial over \(K\) whose splitting field is \(L\). Then

\[d(L/K)=\begin{cases}p,&p\in\{5,7,11\},\\p+1,&p>11.\end{cases}\]
Why the degree classification is complete

For a subgroup \(H\le G\), put \(E=L^H\). The action on \(G/H\) has kernel

\[\operatorname{core}_G(H)=\bigcap_{g\in G}gHg^{-1}.\]

The same intersection fixes the normal closure of \(E/K\) inside \(L\). Every proper subgroup of the simple group \(G\) has trivial core. As \(E/K\) is finite separable, write \(E=K(\alpha)\). The minimal polynomial of \(\alpha\) has degree \([G:H]\) and splitting field \(L\). Conversely, a root of any such irreducible polynomial has a stabilizer of index equal to its degree.

The translation \(x\mapsto x+1\) on \(\mathbb P^1(\mathbb F_p)\) has order \(p\). Any faithful action on \(d\) points embeds \(G\) into \(S_d\), so \(d\ge p\). The natural projective-line action is faithful and transitive, giving degree \(p+1\). Thus the minimum is \(p\) precisely when an index-\(p\) subgroup exists; otherwise it is \(p+1\).

Scope. The extension \(L/K\) is given in advance; this does not assert that the group is realizable over every field. The prime restriction matters: for \(p=2,3\), index-\(p\) subgroups exist but are not core-free, and the corresponding lower-degree equations lose part of the splitting field. The corollary above is deduced from the cited results and the displayed argument; it is not claimed as a new theorem of Pálfy.
